name: Group Attribution Error
description: People overgeneralize between individuals and groups: one member's traits get projected onto the whole group, and a group's actions get projected back onto each member. The shortcut feels efficient but can flatten real within-group differences.
design_relevance_note: Relevant when teams turn a few interviewees into a whole-segment claim, assume one bad actor represents a community, or treat a group decision as if every member believes it equally. It matters in personas, moderation, policy, and research synthesis.
prevalence_note: Recognizable in social-psychology, bias/fairness, and research-methods discussions, but rarely named explicitly in everyday product-design practice.

findings.description: Observers overgeneralize between persons and groups: attributes of an individual member spill over into judgments of the whole group, and attributes or actions of the group spill back onto judgments of its members, even when that inference is not logically warranted.
